Each consequence needs its stated conditions, and the applied-state observation is a consequence of the conditions being met earlier: the partition must have produced two leaders in one term, which in turn needs the two sides physically separated and the restarted side able to reach a quorum of its own reconstruction.
limitations: Single process with in-memory transports and in-memory commit-tracking stores, no crash injection, no disk-backed store and no network fault model beyond the transport's own Disconnect and Connect.

Single-shot windows (200-1600 ms depending on the case, 3000 ms for leadership, 1000-1500 ms for commits) and one or two restarted instances per case; the partition outcome is reproduced twice and the applied divergence is now observed once after healing, but no rate, longer-run or long-stability claim follows.

The applied state is read as the payloads each MockFSM has applied plus each instance's applied position; entries delivered through a snapshot transfer, application-level detection or repair, and a snapshot taken after healing are unexercised.
